subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm deciding to keep this as a static vehicle model without joints, since plain objects don't require a skeleton rig, and sketching out a 6-wheel design to build the geometry under the root.

Now I'm planning the armored truck's components: chassis rails and crossmembers, six treaded wheels with glowing rim rings, wheel arches, an angular extruded cab with a slanted glowing windshield, and a cargo bed topped with a turret, missile pods, antenna, and radar dish.

I'm working out front bumper spikes, light bars, side armor plates, exhaust stacks, fuel tanks, and neon underglow, plus planning 6-8 SVG textures for hazard stripes, decals, stenciled text, and camo patterns, keeping within the 64-color flat palette. I'm also nailing down exact coordinates for the chassis length, cab and cargo zones, and the three wheel axle positions.

Setting up the builder helpers now...

Writing custom panel paint logic...

I'm now working out the windshield as a slanted box, calculating its tilt angle and rotation about the X axis so its normal faces up and forward correctly.

Positioning the windshield plane offset slightly outward along the normal from the slanted roofline midpoint, keeping it within the 1.9-wide span inside the body. Now I'm working out the side window placements on the cab sides, accounting for the roof slope so they fit under the sloped edge at each z-depth.

I'm adding a number decal plane with "77-A" text for the cargo side, then placing dark slat boxes along the sloped hood top for vent details. For the front, I'm sketching a plow/bumper as a wedge-shaped box rotated to match the slope.

Now I'm building the front bumper box and plow blade as an extruded wedge profile with front-facing teeth spikes, then placing glowing headlight boxes near the front face corners.

I'm defining a cyberpunk color palette (cyan, magenta, amber, hazard yellow) and designing a dark front grill with glowing cyan slit boxes positioned below the headlights. For the roof, I'm planning a sensor array with a lidar cylinder, antenna spikes, a light bar, searchlight, and a small lathe-generated dish.

Now I'm shaping the cargo container body with ribbed vertical frames, a roof-mounted rotating rail gun turret with an ammo drum, missile pods with tube arrays on both sides, and rear doors with hazard stripes, tail lights, and a tow hitch.

Still adding side details...

I'll skip skirts and keep the tanks visible with thin strap rings and a neon band. For wheels, I'm setting radius 0.7 with rotated tire cylinders and adding tread blocks as small rotated boxes ringed around the circumference—14 per wheel across 6 wheels, keeping well within the part budget.

Each wheel also needs sidewalls, rim disc, hub, lug nuts, spokes, and a glow ring, bringing the total part count to roughly 460, which still keeps triangle counts manageable since I'm using low-segment cylinders. I'm defining a wheel helper function that builds the rim disc on the outer face with a neon accent ring, considering whether to use a hollow cylinder or ring geometry for that glow effect.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Checking ground contact: with blocks at the bottom (angle 180°, radial down), wheel center at y=0.74 gives tread bottoms around -0.76 to -0.02, which sinks nicely into the floor. I'll set the axle radius at 0.74.

For the tire body, I'm using a cylinder of radius 0.7 and width 0.5, with a mottled dark rubber paint texture for realism. Wheel center sits at y=0.74, with chassis rails around y≈1.0 and cab/cargo bottoms aligned there too.

But now I realize wheels topping out at 1.48 will poke through the body since it bottoms at 1.0 — I need to rework proportions so the deck sits higher (maybe y=1.55) while keeping the cab low enough to still clear the front axle, or shift the wheels outward in x so they protrude through visible wheel arches rather than clipping into the body interior.

Building fender geometry over the wheels using simple tilted boxes rather than curved cylinders to approximate an arch shape.

Now I'm laying out the cargo box height and position relative to the cab roof, then working out where to add underside details like tool lockers and fuel tanks between the axles so there's no visible gap in the chassis.

I'm checking the front and rear wheel positions against the cab and cargo footprint to make sure fenders and arches clear the wheels properly, sizing the fenders to sit just outside the cab width.

Working through the rear end now: checking cargo end placement, bumper box dimensions, tail light positioning, and the hitch assembly, while confirming wheels sink slightly without any geometry dropping below ground level.

Total height comes to about 3.9 with the turret, plus antennas bringing it to 4.4, which feels right. I'm also planning out the SVG texture set I'll need: windshield HUD, side window gradients, a corporate emblem decal, hazard stripes, stenciled unit text, warning decals, and a digital camo paint pattern for the hull.

I'm rounding out the texture list with a neon ARMS-77 sign, a glowing terminal screen with waveform/map graphics for the cargo panel, and skipping the missile pod icon. Writing decal helper function...

Working out the orientation math so text decals face the right way when viewed from outside the model.

Now I'm thinking about adding a glow effect for parts, noting I can apply it to flat colored pieces using the glow utility, and that materials get cloned per color or texture so glow works for both cases.

I need to keep distinct flat colors under 64, and I'm starting to draft the module imports, pulling in the builder, paint utilities, glow and metal kits, plus checking whether helper functions like mix and noise are all exported from a single main module.

Writing hull paint function...

Setting paint texture size to 2048 to fix seam density, then building helper functions for boxes and cylinders to construct the truck's panels with color and placement options.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Adding wheel detail...

Now I'm working out axles, differential, and suspension components—leaf springs and shock absorber rods connecting the axle to the chassis at an angle.

For the cab, I'm extruding a 2D outline into a solid shape along the vehicle's width, then adding details like a roof overhang panel on top.

Working through side skirts, door seams, inset door plates with handles and armor bolt rows, and A-pillar armor plates, plus side mirrors mounted on small boxes near the top of the cab.

Now I'm moving to the hood, laying out front fascia slope, scoop wedges, chevron detailing, and a row of vent slats across the hood surface, plus a magenta glowing ridge strip down the center. Then I'm building the front grill as a dark recessed box with a set of cyan glowing slits for the headlight/vent accents.

Checking wheel positions against bumper width to avoid clipping, then placing a hazard-striped decal on the bumper face and sketching a plow wedge geometry extending forward below the bumper.

Still writing plow shape...

Now I'm adding details: a winch drum cylinder near the bumper top, tow hook boxes, and a roof light bar made of alternating cyan/magenta glow segments, plus a lidar dome cylinder mounted toward the back of the cab roof.

Still shaping roof hardware... I'm adding thin antenna spikes at the rear roof corners and designing a satellite dish using a lathe profile curved into a bowl shape, angled to face up-forward, with a small feed rod positioned at its focal point.

Now I'm building the main cargo box dimensions and position, then layering a roof plate, a darker lower skirt trim, and a repeating series of vertical ribs spaced along the sides for structural detailing.

I also want to place an emblem decal mid-side on the cargo box, but need to skip or adjust nearby ribs so they don't overlap and hide the decal, so I'm working out custom rib spacing that leaves a gap around the decal's position.

I'm also trying to add a stencil text panel like "UNIT 07 / TRK-2077" but keep running into collisions with the rib spacing—shifting it along z and sparsifying the ribs to leave clear space for both elements without clutter.

Settling on final rib positions, decal emblem placement, and two separate text panels (unit ID and hazard warnings) spaced to avoid overlap. I'm also planning glowing neon strips running along the length under the ribs with cyan accents and a thin magenta trim up top.

Now I'm working out the rear hatch and roof details: a maintenance hatch with handle near the text panel, a turret mounted centrally on the roof, and angled missile pods positioned on either side of the cargo top, each built from a rotated box shape to suggest tubes pointing up and back.

Still positioning tube launchers...

Now I'm laying out the turret: a dark cylindrical base with a glowing ring torus around it, a chamfered body built from a main box plus a sloped front section, and twin gun barrels extending forward.

Adding muzzle brakes, cooling shroud rings, glowing rail gun rods running along the barrel, a side ammo box, and a sensor ball with a glowing eye disc. I'm positioning the turret base and computing where its front edge meets the barrel assembly.

Now I'm working on the rear of the vehicle: adding the bumper, door seam details, a hazard decal plane, a glowing rear screen facing backward, and small red glowing tail light boxes positioned symmetrically.

I'm also adding a vertical tail light segment, a license plate with text, and a ladder made of rail boxes and rungs mounted on the rear door. Then I'm figuring out placement for exhaust stacks near the cab-cargo gap, checking that their position doesn't clip into the cargo front face.

Rethinking stack placement outside the cab footprint but on the cargo front face so they clear the window, then moving to figuring out side step plates near the cab door without colliding with the front wheel position.

I'll skip the side steps since they'd conflict with the wheel, and instead work out fender geometry over both wheel pairs—flat top boxes, sloped front/back pieces, and outer lip flares positioned around the front wheels, then apply the same pattern to the rear axle.

Now I'm checking clearances underneath the cargo bed: making sure fender tops stay below the cargo bottom to avoid overlap, then adding chassis rails, cross members, and a drive shaft running between the wheels, all positioned low enough that they're only visible from shallow viewing angles.

I'm placing side fuel tanks between the wheels with cylindrical bodies, mounting straps, end caps, and a glowing neon band, plus checking radius math so they clear the wheel positions in the z-axis.

Then I'm adding magenta underglow strips beneath the chassis and along the skirt bottom edge so they're only visible from below, before moving on to the windshield SVG texture with a dark teal gradient, HUD overlay elements like reticles, brackets, speed readout text, bar charts, and faint reflection streaks.

For the other textures, I'm designing a shield-style emblem with wings and a "77" numeral, a hazard stripe pattern generated programmatically, a stencil decal reading "TRK-2077 UNIT 07" in bold Courier with an outlined off-white color, and a high-voltage warning icon with lightning bolt graphic and "HV 9kV" text placed near the cargo front.

Now I'm planning the remaining decals: a rear terminal screen with a green waveform, grid lines, and radar circle reading "LINK OK," a gradient side window with diagonal reflection stripes, a license plate reading "N77-2077," and a glowing rune-like logo built from paths instead of literal text for the cargo front.

I'm skipping the cargo-front neon since it's mostly hidden by the cab roof, and instead adding a hazard-yellow accent stripe down the center of the cab hull where the surface faces upward, giving the paint scheme a bit more contrast against the gunmetal base.

Adding a magenta racing stripe along the hood/roof, then setting up mirrored loops for left/right sides and writing a small helper function to place geometry parts with position and rotation shorthand.

Writing box, cylinder, and card helpers...

Still working out door seam positions...

Now I'm adding armor plates to the cab sides with small cylinder bolts attached, then noting I should set up the glow material to use an emissive map for textured parts before writing out the full assembly.

I'm defining color constants for the various materials and paints, then starting the hullPaint function that builds the base paint material...

Adding stripe pattern and shading layers...

Adding seam detection using the symmetric offsets, then moving on to positioning the wind deflector plane near the windshield and sketching slanted A-pillar boxes along the windshield edges.

I'm skipping wipers but adding cameras, overhang visor slats above the windshield, a roof hatch circle with a glow ring, and cargo roof details like grille vents, rear antenna whips, and radar placement.

Now I'm positioning the cargo roof elements more precisely — turret, side pods, central radar, hatches, and tall rear antenna spikes — and considering adding a cable harness sweep between the cargo front and turret, though that feels risky and might be skipped.

Switching to the exhaust stacks: dark cylindrical stacks with perforated heat shield bands and glowing orange cap rings, plus bracket boxes and a rain cap, then moving on to winch and suspension rod details.

Writing hazard stripe SVG and emblem SVG...

That's good enough for the badge, so now I'll finalize the design, adding angled "ARMOR" side plates at the cargo's rear top corners and painting "CAB" lettering on the cab roof using the hull paint style.

Adding grill slit spacing, cyan DRL lights, and bull bar posts positioned near the headlights, double-checking the post placements don't overlap the cab width.

Writing wheel function...

Adding wheel details next: lug nuts, hub cap glow, and a brake caliper box peeking through the spokes for extra realism.
